subject: general
question: A small sphere has a radius of 5 cm. A larger sphere is created by uniformly expanding the smaller sphere. The radius of the larger sphere is 15 cm. How many times greater is the surface area of the larger sphere compared to the smaller sphere?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface area ∝ r²

Radius ratio = 15 : 5 = 3 : 1

Area ratio = 3² : 1² = 9 : 1

Larger is 9 times smaller

**∴ Answer = 9 times**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Small sphere radius = 5 cm, Large sphere radius = 15 cm

**Formula used:**

Surface area of sphere = 4πr²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Surface area (small) = 4π × 5² = 100π

⇒ Surface area (large) = 4π × 15² = 900π

⇒ Ratio = 900π : 100π = 9 : 1

**∴ The larger sphere has 9 times the surface area.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of Sphere

Surface area = 4πr²

Scaling Rule

Area changes with square of radius.

Radius Ratio

If radius becomes k times, area becomes k² times.

Volume Note

Volume changes with cube of radius (r³).
